content: Ofloxacin is an antibiotic that is prescribed to treat specific bacterial infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, sexually transmitted infections, and infections of the prostate, skin, and urinary tract. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically administered every 12 hours, with or without food, for a duration of 3 to 10 days, depending on the type and severity of the infection. Certain infections may require treatment for up to 6 weeks or longer. For sexually transmitted infections, a single dose may be sufficient. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Do not alter the dosage or frequency of the medication without medical advice. Swallow the tablets with a full glass of water. Even if you feel better, continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration unless directed otherwise by your doctor. Ofloxacin may also be prescribed for conditions not listed here. If you have questions about other uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting ofloxacin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ofloxacin or other related antibiotics, such as ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, or nalidixic acid. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. This includes antibiotics, blood thinners like warfarin, chemotherapy drugs, cimetidine, cyclosporine, diabetes medications, probenecid, sucralfate, and theophylline. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication regimen or monitor you for potential side effects. If you are taking mineral supplements, antacids containing aluminum, calcium, or magnesium, didanosine, sucralfate, or vitamins with iron or zinc, take ofloxacin at least two hours before or after these substances to avoid interactions. Inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, diabetes, epilepsy, colitis, gastrointestinal issues, vision problems, heart disease, or stroke. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ofloxacin, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking ofloxacin. Be aware that this medication may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fatigue. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen when outdoors. While taking ofloxacin, drink at least eight full glasses of water or other fluids daily to stay hydrated. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Mild side effects of ofloxacin may include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, restlessness, or difficulty sleeping. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face or throat, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, pale or dark stools, blood in the urine, unusual fatigue, severe sunburn, seizures, vaginal infections, vision changes, or tendon pain, inflammation, or rupture. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor promptly. Store ofloxacin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat, moisture, and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or stops breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments while taking ofloxacin. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Inform laboratory personnel that you are taking ofloxacin before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and note that your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of treatment, contact your doctor. The brand name for ofloxacin is Floxin®.
